sentences.text: This pterosaur is defined by a unique skull shape that is very long and low, with the height at the quadrates measuring less than 19% of the total length.
It possesses a blade-like crest on the lower jaw but lacks one on the upper jaw, a combination never seen in other pterosaurs.
The rear edge of this lower jaw crest ends in a distinct hook-like process.
The genus name translates to "Ikran dragon," honoring the jaw-crested creatures from the film Avatar, while the species name makes a second reference to that movie.
Scientists propose the hook on the crest functioned as an anchor for a throat pouch used to store food, much like a pelican.
A second fossil specimen includes a skull, jaws, and the initial three vertebrae of the neck.
Both known examples were recovered from the Aptian-age Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning, dating to roughly 120 million years ago.
The animal was first described in 2014 by Wang Xiaolin and colleagues, though formal naming under ICZN rules did not occur until 2020.
diet: Ikrandraco was a fish-eater living with Liaoningopterus gui and Guidraco venator, yet its smaller, less sturdy teeth indicate it filled a different ecological role.
Scientific analyses place Ikrandraco within the family Lonchodraconidae and identify it as the sister taxon to Lonchodraco.
This creature inhabited the Aptian stage, a period spanning from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
It remains uncertain whether the genus Lonchodectes is valid, as Rodrigues and Kellner argued in 2013 that it was a nomen dubium and moved its species to Lonchodraco.
